doc.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Kenton's Innovations orchestra and the 1952 reorganization
summary: Strings were before his time; many stars left in late 1951 and the band was rebuilt in early 1952.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Were you on the band when he had the — didn’t he have a string section for a while?

Yeah. I think they called that the “Innovations in Modern Jazz” or something, so they called it the Innovations Orchestra. That was, he did two tours with that, I think in ’48 and ’49. That was before me. Then in 1951, at the end of 1951, a lot of people left, Bob Cooper and Bud Shank and Shelly Manne and Shorty Rogers, a lot of the stars left. So when he reorganized the band in early ’52 that’s when I joined. But no strings.
